## U-P300 Sol scan — complete, 2026-09-08

Reconciled U-P300 results: 300/300 (281 clear, 19 confirmed defective). 0 remain.

Owner-requested triage of 300 of the 2005 U-P items. Three Sol (high) agents
have disjoint 100-item assignments in `up300-sol-scan-assignments.json`.
Selection is the first 300 U-P IDs in canonical page/item reading order,
not a predicted-defect or easy-item selection. Each agent reads one item at
a time and consults authoritative full-text sources for unfamiliar mathematics.
`up300-sol-scan-brief.md` records the exact policy and receipt schema.
After each result the agents run `up300-sync-ledger.mjs --apply`: an exclusive
lock serializes apply_patch updates, checks scanned item hashes, and maintains
evidence and counts. It imports agent verdicts; it does not infer them. Stale
bytes or malformed receipts stop the update for reconciliation.

This scan makes no published-content repairs. Completed findings move from
U-P either to the scoped no-repair-needed list or to U-C. Correct implicit
uses of adequate already-published results are NOT defects, even when metadata
omits the link. Unmet prerequisites requiring Phase 3, unjustified premises
and other confirmed mathematical defects go to U-C, not A-P, under the owner's
explicit scan policy. U-C here means pending repair audit; it does not deny
that the item was read during triage. Unresolved uncertainty is not a verdict.
Do not change counts for assignments whose item-specific results have not landed.

### Finite simplicial realization

Target: `prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization`.
The confirmed invalid open-extension step was repaired under the owner's
early-repair authorization; Terra and independent group-f review accepted it.
The repair
embeds the finite vertex
realization in Euclidean space. Each simplex is compact and ambient closed.
A weakly closed set intersects each simplex in an ambient closed set, and is
their finite union. Conversely an ambient closed set restricts to a closed
set on every simplex. Thus weak and subspace topologies agree; finite-union
compactness and the Hausdorff subspace property finish. Include the empty case.
Use the existing compactness/Hausdorff suppliers and prove the finite
closed-cover argument inline. **Do not cite AT-24 here:** AT-24 requires
AT-1, so that proposed cutover would be circular. Its proof is a recipe only.

### Completed-measurable change of variables

Target: `thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions`.
Confirmed generating-class/localization gap; Phase 3 open. At order 288.021,
use the earlier `lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system` (288.003),
continuous compactly supported change of variables, monotone convergence
and completion.

Define Borel measures `mu(E)=lambda(E)` and
`nu(E)=integral_U 1_E(Tx)|det DT(x)| dx`; prove countable additivity by
monotone convergence. Product tent functions increase to indicators of open
boxes compactly contained in V, giving equality and finite mass on those
boxes. Fix such a box Q and restrict both measures to Q. They agree on the
pi-system of relatively compact open boxes, including empty intersections,
which generates the Borel sets of V. Verify equal total masses separately,
then apply finite-measure uniqueness. Cover V by countably many rational
boxes, disjointify the cover and sum to obtain equality on all Borel sets.
An arbitrary open V need not admit an increasing exhaustion by single boxes.
Extend to Lebesgue sets using null preservation for the inverse map, then
simple functions and monotone convergence, including infinite integrals.

**Do not cite** the later Phase-2
`lem-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-borel-functions-via-radon-uniqueness`
(458.0021) or its Radon/RMK prerequisites (288.039) from this earlier page.
That would introduce forward dependence and potentially a page cycle.

the latter's increasing-exhaustion hypothesis must not be assumed for boxes.

### Noetherian/DC repair strategy

Directly read `thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-noetherian-modules`,
`def-noetherian-module`, `def-dependent-choice`, and the sequence definition's
type. The formerly omitted DC dependency and real-sequence typing have now
been repaired under the owner's early authorization. DC uses `def-function`
and is homed immediately after Countable Choice at order 18; the theorem
declares DC and its submodule interfaces. Terra accepted both current texts;
independent audit closure remains pending. Neither issue adds a Phase-2 pair.

After that earlier-home repair, declare `def-dependent-choice` in the
Noetherian theorem. For ACC implying the maximal condition, let S be the
nonempty set of submodules under consideration and define the serial
relation by strict inclusion. DC yields a strictly ascending sequence in S,
contradicting ACC. Finite-generation implies ACC by taking the union and
placing its finitely many generators in one stage. The maximal condition
implies finite generation by applying it to all finitely generated submodules
of a fixed N (including zero), then adjoining one element if the maximal
member is proper. These last two arguments are choice-free. The source is
commutative, but the displayed arguments use only left-submodule operations
and extend to the stated left-module scope without commuting scalars.
Full proof checked: [Conrad, Noetherian Modules](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/noetherianmod.pdf),
Theorem 1.7, pp. 2–3.

Revalidate the four DC consumers in the current-run index after the rehome.
Their headers already name DC; that is not evidence that their entire proofs
have been repaired. Subsequent direct reading of
`lem-noetherian-ring-maximal-element-annihilator-exists` found the expected
nonempty family of annihilator ideals and a valid application of the maximal
condition under explicit DC. No separate local proof defect was found.

`thm-complete-nakayama-lemma` and its completeness definition were also read.
Its coefficient-correction proof is adequate locally: express an element of
I^n M as a finite sum, reduce each module term modulo IM, and collect
coefficients in I^n. DC selects successive corrections; their partial sums
define compatible residues, so completeness of R gives limiting coefficients.
Separatedness of M then kills the residual error. Clarify the phrase about
the “classes of m_i” in I^n M/I^(n+1) M: the m_i themselves need not belong
to I^n M; it is their I^n-weighted combinations that supply the quotient.
No new Phase-2 supplier or additional false-theorem verdict is warranted.
The statement and full alternative proof were checked against
[Stacks, Lemma 10.96.12](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M9).
Both items still inherit the protected DC typing/order repair.
The other two consumers were subsequently read. The maximal-counterexample
argument in `thm-lasker-noether-primary-decomposition` is locally valid under
its stated DC assumption; its irreducible-implies-primary supplier still
needs separate re-audit. The equal-radical merging lemma was read. If needed,
make preservation of irredundancy explicit: a witness for any old component
in a merged block lies in every other block but not in that merged block.

`cor-radical-ideals-as-intersections-of-minimal-primes-noetherian` has a
confirmed omitted direction in Step 2.1. It shows every prime minimal over
I is among the listed primes, but must also prove each inclusion-minimal
listed prime p is minimal over I. For any prime q with I contained in q
contained in p, the finite-product argument gives a listed p_i contained
in q. Minimality of p within the list forces p_i=p, hence q=p. This also
avoids presupposing a separately supplied minimal-prime existence theorem.
Expand the finite-product argument by choosing one element outside q from
each factor if no factor is contained in q; their product contradicts
primality. Only finite choice is involved. No new Phase-2 supplier is needed
for this local completion; the existing DC/order repair remains required.
Do not replace DC by countable choice merely
because the chosen sequence has countably many terms.

at r>0 by the ordinary FTC, then cancel r^(n-1). Step 2.1 also omits the
smooth-convolution supplier. Use the already-published

after extending u by zero from a fixed compactly contained larger ball;

the local convolution samples it. Do not extend u by zero on all of Omega
without checking integrability near its boundary.
For the Taylor step, reflections kill off-diagonal moments, permutations
equalize diagonal moments, and the radial second moment yields
r^2/(n+2) for each normalized diagonal moment. Bound the uniform Peano
remainder by o(r^2). No additional Phase-2 pair is needed. Retain the
polar/choice and chart-measure supplier obligations recorded above; this
published theorem remains unchanged pending that combined repair.

Build state (2026-09-08): these suppliers are scaffolded in batch 5, not
published. Group-e's independent recheck accepts this scaffold. The cutover
must explicitly assume the new HB principle where used; it must not turn

Directly read all ten listed consumer proofs, plus
`cor-annihilator-detects-closure` (not yet its separation supplier's proof).
Their local algebraic arguments are sound with adequate HB suppliers; the
repair is dependency/axiom accounting, not a claim these statements are false.
Recommended strategies after the exact suppliers above publish:

- Real/complex extension: apply the relative extension theorem without adding
  closedness of the subspace or completeness of the ambient space. If retaining
  the complex reconstruction, use U(x)-iU(ix); rotate a nonzero scalar value
  by its conjugate divided by its modulus to obtain the sharp norm bound,
  treating zero separately. This avoids introducing an exponential argument
  merely to select a phase.
- Norming: define the functional on the one-dimensional span of a nonzero x
  by sending a*x to a*norm(x), then extend. For the dual-unit-ball formula at
  x=0 use the zero functional; do not require a norm-one functional in a zero
  space. Point separation applies norming to the difference of the points.
- Transpose: composition gives the upper norm bound. For each fixed x with
  Tx nonzero apply one norming functional to Tx for the reverse bound; no
  simultaneous choice of functionals indexed by all x is needed.
- Annihilators: the first identity is algebraic; the second uses norming to
  detect Tx=0. The closure identity also needs the existing
  `cor-annihilator-detects-closure`, whose separate separation proof must be
  revalidated under HB. Norming alone does not prove that closure statement.
- Bidual: evaluation gives contraction; one norming functional gives equality
  for each nonzero x. Keep scalar-linear evaluation without conjugation, and
  do not infer surjectivity/reflexivity from isometry.
- Open-set separation: apply the relative geometric theorem to the open set
  and the singleton outside it, retaining pointwise strict separation and a
  nonzero functional. Do not upgrade this to a uniform positive gap for an
  arbitrary open set. The existing gauge proof also works under HB: translate
  the set, dominate a functional on the line to the outside point, and use a
  contained norm ball to prove continuity. The current theorem already says
  AC; replacing that stronger assumption by HB must be explicit, not silent.

uses existing `thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives` and

needed for this local route, and no sigma-finiteness assumption need be added
to the theorem. Keep `C=B+eta` and its limiting argument, which already handles

proof-interface repair, not a counterexample to the theorem's conclusion.

#### Scaffold III.4.2 — Skolem construction

The old §29.3 blocker is resolved.  Meszka's full 22-page design-theory lecture
notes give the complete Skolem construction on printed pp. 9--10, including all
blocks.  Before the published existence theorem on
`block-designs-and-finite-projective-planes`, insert, in this order:

1. `def-half-idempotent-commutative-quasigroup`;
2. `lem-cyclic-even-set-carries-a-half-idempotent-commutative-quasigroup`;
3. `thm-skolem-construction-produces-a-steiner-triple-system`.

For $v=6k+1$, take $Q=\{0,\ldots,2k-1\}$, a half-idempotent commutative
quasigroup, and $V=(Q\times\{1,2,3\})\cup\{\infty\}$.  The proof must check
pair coverage for the vertical blocks
`{(i,1),(i,2),(i,3)}` for $0\le i<k$, the three infinity blocks
`{∞,(k+i,1),(i,2)}`, `{∞,(k+i,2),(i,3)}`,
`{∞,(k+i,3),(i,1)}`, and, for $i<j$, the three cyclic layer blocks
`{(i,1),(j,1),(i∘j,2)}` and its $1\to2\to3\to1$ rotations.  Replace the
dependency of
`thm-steiner-triple-systems-exist-exactly-when-v-congruent-one-or-three-mod-six`
on `rem-skolem-construction-produces-a-steiner-triple-system` by the new theorem.
The old remark may remain only as non-load-bearing history.

The quasigroup-existence lemma is elementary and must be proved, not imported:
start with the addition table of $\mathbb Z/(2k)$.  Its diagonal entries are
$2i$, so each even residue occurs exactly twice, at $i$ and $i+k$.  Relabel the
even output $2r$ by $r$ for $0\le r<k$, and relabel the odd outputs bijectively
by $k,\ldots,2k-1$.  Output relabelling preserves the Latin and commutative
properties and gives diagonal entries $r$ at both $r$ and $r+k$.  Thus every
input used by the Skolem verification is local and proved.

For the three new supplier items, the currently published consumer ledger is:

| `def-half-idempotent-commutative-quasigroup` | zero (its immediate consumers are new repair items) | `thm-steiner-triple-systems-exist-exactly-when-v-congruent-one-or-three-mod-six` |
| `lem-cyclic-even-set-carries-a-half-idempotent-commutative-quasigroup` | zero (its immediate consumer is a new repair item) | `thm-steiner-triple-systems-exist-exactly-when-v-congruent-one-or-three-mod-six` |
| `thm-skolem-construction-produces-a-steiner-triple-system` | `thm-steiner-triple-systems-exist-exactly-when-v-congruent-one-or-three-mod-six` | same singleton |

not supply a bounded replacement.  The full Annals proof of SPGT is 178 pages,
and GT-13 correctly denies it as a subject-scale theorem.  Therefore
`thm-neighbourhood-or-antineighbourhood-of-a-vertex-in-a-basic-bull-free-graph-is-perfect`
cannot be repaired within this scaffold.  The unrepaired supplier
`rem-strong-perfect-graph-theorem-for-the-bull-route` has the direct published
consumer
`thm-neighbourhood-or-antineighbourhood-of-a-vertex-in-a-basic-bull-free-graph-is-perfect`;
its full transitive published consumer closure is:

## 53. Compliant Computability Phase-2 replacement pairs

Binding source: `research/plan-computability-theory-track.md` §53. The original
five-pair replacement inventory had 30 A and 13 B items. The UC-73 audit adds
one A theorem there and the A626.2/B626.4 pair
`nondeterministic-recursive-padding-and-time-separation` / its `-examples`
page: the current six-pair inventory has 38 A and 15 B items. Every B is a leaf.
All 55 old draft IDs remain Phase-3 cleanup on their ten published pages.

The new pair supplies `thm-nondeterministic-time-hierarchy`: constructibility
alone does not prove nondeterministic separation. Its seven A obligations
cover linear nondeterministic simulation, time-controlled self-reference,
cutoffs/unions, unary diagonalization and recursive padding; two B examples
test the interface. The canonical plan registers the pages with empty item
arrays until scaffolding; neither registration nor an external citation is a
proof. The Phase-2 manifest now has 144 pairs (19 active, 125 waiting).

Existing A612.2 additionally must prove
`thm-clocked-universal-simulation-with-time-and-space-bounds` before repairing
`def-efficient-universal-simulation-with-clock` and its time-diagonal
consumers. The binding contract uses TWO interpreters: a buffered time
simulator and a configuration-scanning space simulator, with separate bounds;
it does not assume a single jointly optimal interpreter. Source and exact
contracts are in prose §53.1 and the UC-73 evidence below. These are unbuilt
proof obligations, not discharged prerequisites. Later local-repair verdicts
in the classification index supersede the historical consumer edges below.

For an old ID `x`, `Impact(x)` means its exact direct and complete transitive
published-consumer row in §52 above; unions are deduplicated by item ID. This
keeps the existing 47-consumer/55-edge map exact. The replacement map is:

## 7.5 Cross-category ownership seams

- Category Theory owns accessible/presentable categories and accessibility
  machinery. SET-4's “accessible pointed graph” is only the membership-graph
  notion. Its Grothendieck-universe items neither assert an inaccessible exists
  nor supply a category-theoretic universe-change theorem.
- Abstract Algebra owns rings, ideals, quotients and homomorphism algebra.
  SET-7 defines Boolean algebras and Boolean ideals for Stone/BPI and must prove
  its bridge explicitly; a commutative-ring prime-ideal theorem is not BPI.
  Algebraic Geometry owns `Spec` and schemes; Stone spectrum is not scheme
  spectrum.
- `fs-ordinals-form-a-set` has exactly two direct and transitive published
  consumers, both on
  `reflective-subcategories-and-the-adjoint-functor-theorems-examples`:
  `cex-a-category-that-is-not-well-powered` and
  `cex-a-complete-category-whose-coseparating-sets-are-never-small`.
  `fs-every-ultrafilter-principal` has exactly one direct/transitive consumer,
  `ex-the-ultrafilter-monad-on-a-finite-set`, on
  `monads-comonads-and-their-algebras-examples`. These suppliers are A-homed in
  the canonical spec and therefore do not violate B-leaf discipline.
- The real-analysis home of DC and the topology continuum repair are binding
  interfaces. A missing A input must never be patched by adding it directly to
  a Foundations B page.

## 7.6 Full-text evidence and source blockers

- S. Feferman, *Some applications of the notions of forcing and generic sets*,
  Fundamenta Mathematicae 56 (1964/65), 325--345, DOI
  `10.4064/fm-56-3-325-345`: the full publisher scan was recovered. Theorem
  4.12 and proof, printed pp. 343--344, use finitely many generic-set parameters
  and a tail-complement transform of the next generic set to contradict a
  supposed nonprincipal prime ideal. This is the authoritative correction to
  the invalid finite-bit-flip summary.
- M. Morillon, *The power of DMC*, full author PDF, p. 6, records that DMC plus
  countable choice for finite sets implies DC. The full Japanese note *On
  dependent choice*, Definition and Propositions 6--7, PDF pp. 4--5, confirms
  the finite-level formulation and prescribed-start equivalence. The published
  SET-6 proof supplies the easy converse directions directly.
- A. Blass, *A model without ultrafilters*, Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. 25 (1977),
  329--331: bibliographic identity and a later primary-author confirmation were
  recovered, but no authoritative full text of the proof was accessible.
  `thm-blass-model-has-only-principal-ultrafilters` remains **blocked**;
  secondary summaries are not proof sources.
- Andretta--Notaro, *Does DC imply AC_omega uniformly?*, JSL (2024), full
  Cambridge PDF, §5.2, printed pp. 1560--1561, confirms the Feferman--Levy
  consequence used for orientation but does not replace the required original
  symmetric-model construction. SET-20 remains gated on full construction.

  definition used by its Verma example.

  no HA B page is a supplier.

  laundered through a Lie orientation remark.

  active Computability incoming Linear Algebra interface is disjoint from this

  is removed by the Lie-owned finite-Weyl definition. No other repaired

### Authoritative full-text evidence and blocker

- Pavel Etingof, MIT 18.757 complete notes,
  <https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-757-representations-of-lie-groups-fall-2023/mit18_757_f23_lec_full.pdf>:
  Exercise 8.15(iv)--(x), printed pp.45--47, gives the leading term,
  affine-root-hyperplane factors, generic radical/submodule/quotient,
  transverse perfect derivative pairing, vanishing order, and determinant
  exponent used by the four Phase-3 Shapovalov lemmas. Sections 10--13,
  especially Theorem 13.5 on printed pp.74--75 and its §§13.1--13.2 setup on
  pp.71--74, give the finite reflection-invariant and Kostant harmonic/freeness
  chain. This is full text, not a snippet.
- Pavel Etingof, complete Lie groups/algebras notes,
  <https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/lnlg.pdf>: §§18.1--18.2, printed pp.83--86
  (Lemma 18.5, Proposition 18.6, Theorems 18.7 and 18.10), give the
  regular-element/Cartan-conjugacy argument; §§24.2--24.3, printed pp.107--109
  (Propositions 24.10/24.12, Lemmas 24.15/24.16, Theorem 24.17), give the
  finite-dimensional highest-weight existence, dominance, integrability,
  finite-dimensionality, and uniqueness chain.
- The same official 18.757 notes, Theorem 15.11 on printed p.82, prove the
  generic positive-root Verma embedding from the determinant but give the
  arbitrary case only by the phrase “taking the limit.” No authoritative full
  proof of that specialization was retrieved. This is a blocker, not
  permission to record the claim or to infer it from the theorem statement.

`library/`, `items/`, generated output, or `research/plan-spec.json`.

### 30.1 Immutable snapshot and audit method

The live Group Theory band consists of **23 A pages, 23 B pages, and 842/842
present item files**, all with `status: published`: 171 definitions, 103
lemmas, 57 propositions, 139 theorems, 61 corollaries, 35 remarks, 132
examples, 30 counterexamples, and 114 false statements. The first pair is
stored under `library/abstract-algebra/`; the other 22 are under
`library/group-theory/`. The live item graph is acyclic. It has 22 edges to a
B-page item, but all 22 stay inside the same B page; no B item supplies an A
page or a different B page. Thus the item graph respects page-level leafness,
whereas the page graph does not: it contains B-as-supplier `requires` edges.
This does **not** certify mathematical closure: 20 Group Theory items are explicitly
`proof: not-supplied`/`proved_here: false`, and several nominally proved items
merely invoke their own conclusion as an unlinked source assumption.

historical inventories above. Against the current plan ledger, 161 published
GT items disagree on `deps`: published headers contain 306 edges missing from
the ledger, while the ledger contains 176 edges missing from published
headers. Phase 3 must first repair the mathematical edges specified here and
then replace the ledger dependency list of each GT item verbatim by its repaired
published header. It must not take either side of the present drift as
authoritative merely because the syntactic validators accept it.

HG-18 packages the preceding clauses with their constants and hypotheses so
published agreement theorems can depend on one earlier result. Properness is
used only for compact boundary statements; local finiteness is stated where a
finite ball is counted. “Elementary” means finite or virtually cyclic. The
centralizer conclusion is for finitely generated hyperbolic groups, not
arbitrary groups acting on a hyperbolic space. The Dehn clause
attaches every null loop of length at most `10 delta` and proves both finite
presentability and the shortening property. The boundary clauses specify the
Gromov-product convention and all additive constant changes.

### 30.8 Authoritative full-text evidence and blockers

- Cornelia Druţu and Michael Kapovich, *Geometric Group Theory*, complete
  author-hosted manuscript,
  <https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~kapovich/EPR/kapovich_drutu.pdf>: Chapter 9,
  especially Theorem 9.38 (Morse), Theorems 9.83--9.89 (boundary extension),
  §§9.11--9.13 and Theorem 9.108/Proposition 9.109/Lemma 9.112 (hyperbolic
  groups, linear filling, and Dehn presentations); §12.5, Definition 12.42,
  Proposition 12.43, Lemma 12.44, Proposition 12.45 and Theorem 12.48 (the
  complete Bass--Guivarc'h proof). The whole 585-page text was obtained and
  the cited proof ranges read.
- Matthias Hamann, *Geometric Group Theory*, complete author text,
  <https://www.math.uni-hamburg.de/home/hamann/Lehre/GeoGrTh/GeoGrThEn.pdf>:
  Proposition 5.2.5 and Theorem 5.2.6 prove undistortion and the virtually
  cyclic centralizer; Theorems 5.3.7--5.3.8 prove the general (torsion-allowed)
  boundary trichotomy and rank-two free-subgroup conclusion.
- Richard Canary, *Anosov Representations: Informal Lecture Notes*, complete
  author-hosted text, <https://websites.umich.edu/~canary/lecnotespublic.pdf>:
  Proposition 4.3/Corollary 4.4 and Proposition 5.1 prove infinite cyclic
  undistortion and north--south dynamics; Theorem 7.3 gives the ping-pong
  proof. Its subgroup corollaries explicitly impose torsion-freeness, which is
  why it is not used to certify the two finite-torsion claims isolated in
  §30.4.
- Clara Löh, *Geometric Group Theory: An Introduction*, complete author text,
  <https://loeh.app.uni-regensburg.de/teaching/ggt_ws1415/lecture_notes_old.pdf>:
  the growth and quasi-isometry sections were used as independent convention
  control. Its Bass theorem is a statement with a reference, not the proof
  source for BG, and this edition was not used for small cancellation.
- Nicholas Touikan, *An Introduction to Combinatorial and Geometric Group
  Theory*, complete author HTML, §3.5,
  <https://ntouikan.ext.unb.ca/MATH6022/IntroCGGT/html_output/section-18.html>:
  arc reduction, pieces, shells, and Proposition 3.5.5. This supports SC-1--SC-6.
- Roger C. Lyndon and Paul E. Schupp, *Combinatorial Group Theory*, Chapter V,
  §10, Theorem 10.1 and Lemma 10.2, Springer (1977/2001), complete searchable
  scan, pp. 281--282: the relator-power piece criterion, shortest-conjugate
  argument, Greendlinger application, repeated-period case, and shorter-
  conjugate contradiction close SC-7--SC-9. The earlier source blocker is
  resolved.
- Peter Webb, *A Course in Finite Group Representation Theory*, complete
  author-hosted text,
  <https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~webb/RepBook/RepBookLatex.pdf>, and the
  complete Meier Brauer-character notes,
  <https://users.math.msu.edu/users/meierfra/Classnotes/MTH912F04/913S05notes.pdf>,
  §6.4, especially Lemma 6.4.3. The latter prints the separation-and-trace

The live plan has 44 Probability pages.  PT-1--PT-5 are ten published pages
with 166 items: respectively A/B counts 30/11, 22/6, 21/8, 23/9, and 27/9
(123 A items and 43 B items).  PT-6--PT-22 are 34 empty planned pages.  All
134 published proof-bearing Probability items pass the scoped precheck.  Every
declared direct item dependency resolves to a published item, and the complete
transitive closure of all 166 published items contains zero
`proved_here: false` items and zero unresolved items.

These invariants are binding for every later build:

1. No definition, theorem, proof, `deps`, `justified_by`, or load-bearing body
   link may directly or transitively use a recorded-but-unproved or
   not-proved-here claim.  An orientation sentence cannot launder such a claim.
2. Every B page requires only its A companion.  No item may depend on a B item,
   and no page or item may consume a B page or item.  Thus every B page is a
   dependency leaf, not a bridge to the next pair.
3. Every A input must be adequate, published at build time, and strictly
   earlier.  A later or empty page supplies nothing.
4. Phase 2 may add new A/B supplier pairs only.  Nothing placed on an already
   published PT-1--PT-5 page is Phase-2 work.

Durrett Theorem 2.1.22 (pp. 53--54) supplies the explicit Hilbert-cube/digit
coding route.  The proof must spell out the canonical-expansion convention,
the Borel description of the code image, and measurability of the inverse;
the book itself warns that its printed proof is light on those details.  The
published topology embedding and Polish-$G_\delta$ theorems supply the needed
Borel-image step.  Do not build PT-11 unless those details pass proof review.

Before PT-11 item 8 add
`lem-simultaneous-rational-conditional-distribution-function-versions` and
`lem-rational-conditional-distribution-functions-produce-real-regular-kernels`.
They must follow Durrett Theorem 4.1.17 (pp. 214--215): select conditional CDF
versions only at rational cuts; discard one countable union of null sets;
right-regularize by an infimum over rationals; invoke the proved
CDF-to-measure correspondence; then use a pi--lambda argument for measurable
kernel evaluation.  Pull the real kernel back through the earlier
bimeasurable coding.  Before disintegration add
`lem-regular-conditional-kernels-factor-through-a-standard-borel-conditioning-variable`,
using the Phase-3 Doob--Dynkin theorem and the countable determining algebra,
as in Durrett Theorem 4.1.18 (p. 215).  The old sentence “choose versions on a
countable algebra and extend” is not an adequate proof: arbitrary separately
chosen versions do not automatically give countably additive sections.

Retire both planned pathology remarks
`rem-regular-conditional-probability-existence-boundary` and
`rem-nonstandard-space-failure-of-regular-conditionals` as items.  Preserve
only the non-load-bearing, unlinked scope sentence that PT-11 proves existence
under its stated standard-Borel hypothesis and makes no claim beyond it.
Likewise rewrite PT-6 item 13 to say only that the stated strong law contains
no rate assertion, PT-8 item 11 to say only that the derivative lemma has no
converse in this track, and PT-22 item 15 to say that Stratonovich integration
and any conversion theorem are not developed.  These formulations record no
unproved mathematical result.

### 0A.5 Choice-strength correction and Foundations seam

The supplied published countable-product proof explicitly assumes both
`def-countable-choice` and `def-dependent-choice`; its actual upper bound is
ZF + DC + $\mathsf{AC}_\omega$, not the stale “$\mathsf{AC}_\omega$ inherited
from MT-3” row.  The published arbitrary-index standard-Borel theorem
explicitly assumes full `def-axiom-of-choice` to select one Polish
presentation for every coordinate and to fill inactive coordinates.  Its
actual supplied upper bound is AC, not BPI.  Consequently PT-15's path-law
route inherits DC + $\mathsf{AC}_\omega$, and PT-18's presently planned
arbitrary-time-index Brownian construction inherits AC.  No lower bound or
reverse implication is asserted.

The Foundations-owned Phase-3 repair must rehome `def-dependent-choice` to
`countability-and-uncountability` immediately after `def-countable-choice`,
replace its inapplicable `def-sequence` dependency/body link by `def-function`,
and reconcile the consumers below.  It must also remove the stronger
`def-axiom-of-choice` dependency from the *definitions* of the weaker choice
principles unless a statement genuinely assumes AC; descriptive comparison
remarks are not hypotheses.  Probability may consume the axiom definitions
but may not consume the recorded relative-consistency remarks in their
bodies.  Until a proved implication item exists, a theorem using both DC and
$\mathsf{AC}_\omega$ must state both rather than cite an unproved orientation
claim that DC implies countable choice.

### 0A.7 Cross-category ownership seams

Measure Theory owns sigma-algebras, measures, measurable functions, Lebesgue
integration, convergence in measure/a.e., finite products and Fubini--Tonelli,
Radon--Nikodym, scalar $L^p$, Radon regularity, and the ergodic theorems.
Probability owns laws, independence, infinite probability products,
conditional expectation as the RN application, conditional kernels,
martingales, Markov chains, Brownian motion, and Brownian Ito calculus.  The
new standard-Borel coding pair uses topology's Polish/Hilbert-cube machinery
but remains Probability-owned because it supplies Probability's existing
`def-standard-borel-space` interface.  Functional Analysis owns finite-measure
Fourier uniqueness and continuous functional calculus; Probability only
specializes them.  Combinatorics owns the finite probability pages.  No seam
is allowed to route through an examples companion.

Authoritative full text inspected for the nonroutine repair: Rick Durrett,
*Probability: Theory and Examples*, 5th ed., Theorem 2.1.22, pp. 53--54
(standard-Borel/“nice” coding), and Theorems 4.1.17--4.1.18, pp. 214--215

#### 1. cor-dimension-birational-invariant — A-P

Original concern: draft `thm-birational-equivalence-function-fields`. Read entire consumer, that theorem, birational definition, published open-dimension proof and chart-field proof. The conclusion and restriction argument are mathematically sound conditional on those interfaces. Local simplification can remove the affine field theorem by defining birationality through inverse maps and shrinking to inverse isomorphic opens; it does not close the unpublished rational-map interface or the open-dimension supplier's dependency on draft field identifications. Thus defer the prerequisite repair, without claiming the theorem false.

Exact S suppliers: `def-classical-birational-equivalence`, `thm-classical-birational-equivalence-iff-function-fields-isomorphic`; indirect chart repair needs `thm-classical-function-field-independent-of-affine-open` and `lem-classical-dominant-map-pulls-back-function-fields`. Existing replacement birational files are draft. Recommended Phase-3 proof: explicitly shrink inverse rational representatives to common isomorphic opens, then apply repaired open invariance. Source: Milne §5l, Proposition 5.39 (printed p.117). AC is inherited through the field/dimension interfaces; consumer asserts AC but lacks `def-axiom-of-choice`, so Phase 3 must declare it and identify inherited use rather than invent a new choice step. Files changed: this receipt only. No new missing Phase-2 scope identified. Downstream claims are impact candidates, not separately audited defects.

#### 2. cor-module-finite-affine-map-quasi-finite — A-P

Read complete consumer and all four direct contracts, including the Nullstellensatz proof. The finite-dimensional algebra argument is valid: any finite collection of distinct maximal ideals yields that many independent CRT residue vectors, bounding the collection size. Empty fibres are handled. Crucially, surjectivity of the point/maximal-ideal correspondence is unnecessary: distinct classical points already yield distinct evaluation kernels, so the direct Nullstellensatz call can be removed locally in a later rewrite. This does not close the draft morphism/coordinate-ring interface behind the module-finite and fibre definitions. No false theorem found.

S suppliers: `thm-classical-affine-nullstellensatz-correspondence` (current direct F4/reduced-fibre interface; draft), `thm-classical-affine-algebraic-sets-reduced-algebras-antiequivalence` (reducible/empty module-finite source and target), `def-classical-affine-variety-morphism`, `def-classical-regular-map-image-and-set-theoretic-fibre` (all S drafts). Repair strategy: retain finite-dimensional CRT proof, use point evaluation injections directly, and bind definitions to the new algebraic-set/morphism interface after publication. This elementary finite CRT argument uses no arbitrary choice; the current blanket AC clause is inherited, and its dependency/use must be made explicit only if the repaired interface still uses AC. Source research was unnecessary for the elementary algebra; the full local CRT proof was checked, not treated as an external black box. Files changed: receipt only; no precheck/rendercheck required or claimed; no new Phase-2 scope. Audit does not certify suppliers' whole closures.

#### 6. def-product-varieties-universal-property — A-P

Resumed after checking this receipt and current files. Read entire item, categorical product and affine/projective-set contracts, and the affine product consumer. The restricted category is legitimate; it deliberately does not assert existence for mixed factors, so the familiar nonprojective/nonaffine mixed-product obstruction is not a defect. The universal property is the correct one for all test objects in that category. Empty and point cases are sound. Sol 1; scanned SHA-256: `804033d39243fa4713c490ce391b6438e26050d6b7aebb998eee296d73da12dd`.

Scope: Read the complete theorem and proof; checked existence of a minimal normal subgroup, the automorphism orbit construction, characteristic closure, irredundant direct-factor criterion, simplicity of factors, finiteness, and isomorphism.

Findings:

- Finiteness supplies a minimal nontrivial normal subgroup and finitely many automorphic images. Their generated subgroup is nontrivial characteristic, hence all of characteristically simple G.
- Distinct orbit members centralize; an irredundant generating subfamily has each factor intersecting the product of the others trivially by minimal normality, giving an internal direct product.
- Any normal subgroup of one factor is normalized by that factor and centralized by all others, hence normal in G; minimal normality makes the factor simple. Automorphic images are pairwise isomorphic.

### ex-simple-diagonal-action — clear

Sol 1; scanned SHA-256: `5fbc9a1ec534eb34ca0f100a5747977ae493b0ecc06c9c046f9e677537f22cec`.

Scope: Read the complete example and verification; checked the socle, point stabilizer, maximality argument, primitivity criterion, diagonal-type definition, and whether the defective O'Nan–Scott dependency is actually used.

Findings:

- For nonabelian simple T, the socle of T×T is the product of its two simple direct factors and the stabilizer of the identity coset is Δ(T).
- If L properly contains Δ(T), it contains (1,x) with x≠1; diagonal conjugation generates 1×T by simplicity, and Δ(T)(1×T)=T×T. Thus Δ(T) is maximal and the coset action primitive.
- These facts directly meet the diagonal-type definition. The declared O'Nan–Scott theorem dependency is unused metadata, so its separate proof defect does not infect this direct example under the owner's rule.

### thm-dehn-algorithm-solves-the-word-problem — clear

Sol 1; scanned SHA-256: `53e52222acbaa9a18f5ed4eb0e8241d66febbc8d639aaae3bf518b1f00edc4ea`.

Scope: Read the complete theorem/proof, the Dehn-presentation definition, strict-shortening lemma, and declared Greendlinger/van Kampen dependencies; checked termination, group-element preservation, both correctness directions, and actual dependency use.

Findings:

- Each replacement plus free reduction strictly decreases a natural-number word length, so the algorithm terminates.
- Relator replacement preserves the presented group element; reaching the empty word therefore proves triviality.
- Conversely, the defining contract of a Dehn presentation itself says every nonempty freely reduced trivial word admits another move, so termination cannot occur nonempty on a trivial input. The U-C Greendlinger theorem is declared but not used: it is needed to prove C'(1/6) presentations are Dehn, not this general theorem for an already-assumed Dehn presentation.

Findings:

- The action of S4 on the three pair partitions has kernel exactly the identity plus the three double transpositions, hence V4; restriction to H has kernel H∩V4 and image order |H|/|H∩V4|.
- Transitivity forces 4|H| and Lagrange gives |H| in {4,8,12,24}. These yield S4; the unique index-two A4; Sylow-2 subgroups conjugate to D4; and, in the regular order-four case, C4 or the fixed-point-free double-transposition V4. This proves exhaustiveness up to conjugacy.
- Direct intersection counts are 4,4,4,2,4, giving pairing images S3,A3,C2,C2,1. Parity correctly places only A4 and V4 inside A4; standard D4 has odd reflections and C4 an odd four-cycle.

Intervals nest, halve in length, and have a unique common point c; both endpoint sequences converge to c. Continuity sends their values to f(c), and non-strict order preservation squeezes f(c)=y.

### lem-real-and-metric-notions-agree — clear

Sol 3; scanned SHA-256: `edcafbcc141502bf3acd16dfb37cb17efe9dfb6f07c99d55e1036e2a44ecb7a4`.

Scope: All seven dictionary clauses checked against the real and metric definitions, including intrinsic compactness, convergence, regularity hierarchy and Cauchy transfer.

Findings:

- Continuity, uniform continuity, Lipschitz and Holder conditions reduce literally to the same absolute-value formulas under the usual subspace metric. Ambient-open-cover compactness matches compactness of the metric subspace by the intrinsic compactness lemma, and sequential convergence agrees termwise. The regularity and Cauchy consequences therefore transfer through published metric theorems.

### thm-heine-cantor-r — clear

Sol 3; scanned SHA-256: `8538b8b411795af77f6ab30d886770d49862b0c82fdf45572fc951b9cfe16344`.

Scope: Full contradiction proof, paired bad-point selection, sequential compactness extraction, second-sequence convergence and exact choice cost checked.

Findings:

- Failure of uniform continuity gives a nonempty bad-pair set at each radius 1/(k+1); one application of countable choice selects the pairs. Sequential compactness extracts a convergent subsequence of first coordinates, while shrinking pair distances force the matching second coordinates to the same p. Choice-free sequential continuity sends both image subsequences to f(p), contradicting their uniform epsilon_0 separation.

### thm-compactness-is-necessary-for-evt-and-uniform-continuity — U-C

Sol 3; scanned SHA-256: `68ae103c378e8b6551f7766db76d65bbec26fb5b0494c64157e34b1bf55aec33`.

Scope: All three formal claims and four witness proofs checked; formal claims are valid, but two surrounding global/choice assertions are confirmed false.

Findings:

- Immediately after claims 1-3, the paragraph says that on every noncompact set 'each of those three conclusions fails for some continuous function' and that compactness is exactly the hypothesis uniform continuity needs. This is false for unbounded uniformly discrete noncompact sets such as E=Z: every function E->R is uniformly continuous by taking delta<1. Rudin Theorem 4.20 explicitly restricts the non-uniform-continuity conclusion to bounded E and explicitly gives the integers as the counterexample if boundedness is omitted.
- The second Remarks bullet says the claim-3 extension argument 'spends none' because cor-continuous-extension-from-a-dense-subset-r constructs without selection. That corollary and its metric supplier actually inherit AC_omega through Cantor intersection and metric sequential closure. Thus this item repeats the substantive false choice-freedom claim confirmed in item 97. The formal witness proofs remain correct under authorized AC.

Phase-3 prose must retain the boundedness restriction instead of globally characterizing compactness for uniform continuity..

Repair strategy: Revise the summary to say claims 1 and 2 characterize failure on every noncompact E, while failure of uniform continuity is guaranteed only when E is bounded and noncompact; mention unbounded uniformly discrete sets as the obstruction. Replace the no-choice remark with the supplier's accurate AC_omega accounting. Keep the four correct witness proofs.

### Classification rules and Phase-3 completion gate

- Audit status concerns the **current repair finding**, not the old publication
  stamp. A-R and A-P mean a recorded defect-focused review (structural or semantic,
  as specified per row), not a full
  transitive mathematical audit. Preserve the review scope in the evidence.
- U-P is a conservative reconciliation queue. It includes supplier-only mentions,
  downstream impact candidates, prior bounded no-defect findings, and older
  category findings whose item-specific disposition has not yet been migrated.
  It does **not** assert these items have never been read or are all suspect
  proofs. A recorded confirmed finding above must not be erased or downgraded
  merely because migration into this index remains pending.
- U-C rows identify confirmed repair debt pending repair audit: an exact
  unmet prerequisite, unjustified proof use or other demonstrated mathematical
  defect. In the U-P300 scan, all such findings enter U-C by owner instruction,
  including prerequisites deferred to Phase 3. Correct implicit use of an
  adequate published supplier is clear, not a metadata-only defect. Mere
  supplier-page proximity does not establish debt, and a planned supplier is
  not published. A prerequisite defect need not make the theorem false.
- A-R closes only the recorded repair. A later independent defect reopens the
  item in A-P (or U-C while its proof audit is incomplete). Do not close a
  published proof because its scaffold or supplier was repaired.
- A-P is the reconciled Phase-3 repair queue. U-C is also confirmed repair
  debt and must be audited into A-P, or repaired with evidence, before Phase 2
  closes. U-P is an audit/reconciliation backlog, not a repair total.
- Maintain one row per canonical published item ID. Move its row when status
  changes; retain the evidence, exact Phase-2 suppliers and repair strategy
  above. Update counts after every move or new finding. Multiple findings
  on one item stay open until all are resolved.
- At Phase-2 completion, reconcile **every published item**, all category
  reports and all engine findings. Resolve U-P/U-C dispositions; keep an
  explicit reviewed/no-repair-needed receipt for cleared reference-only or
  sound items outside the four active defect classes. Do not relabel a sound
  item as repaired. Freeze a deduplicated A-P list with exact supplier IDs,
  publication states, proof strategies and evidence. No unresolved premise
  may lack a Phase-2 or already-published supplier (or an explicit local proof).
- **Migration remains incomplete.** The counts below are classifications of
  known references, not final repair totals. In particular A-P plus U-C is
  a lower bound on recorded repair debt until older category findings are
  reconciled. Do not claim complete discovery or Phase-3 readiness yet.
